book.eternal_starlight.seeking_eye: A magical eye that can be used to locate the ruins where the powerful creatures live. You need to hold a locator item too if you wish to find a specific structure.
book.eternal_starlight.orb_of_prophecy:
A mysterious orb that knows all.
It can be used on the portal frame to open the portal.
Beside from this, you can access all of your crests and cast spells with them.
To cast a spell, first check the requirements of the spell you want to cast and make sure you have one of the mana crystals that can be accepted.
Then, hold the orb and switch to that spell you want to cast.
Lastly, you're ready to use the orb to cast the spell.
book.eternal_starlight.accessories.title: Accessories
book.eternal_starlight.accessories:
Accessories are items that can be combined with equipments to grant unique properties. Each accessory can only be combined with a specific type of equipment.
The number of accessories an equipment can hold depends on the number of accessory slots it possesses. You can combine or separate accessories from equipment just as you would place or remove items from a bundle. Additionally, combining can be done directly through crafting. When an item's durability is depleted, all combined accessories will be lost.
Accessories may be obtained from mobs or chests. Additionally, some accessories have unique acquisition methods.
book.eternal_starlight.accessories.butte: Throw any accessory into the Ether
book.eternal_starlight.starlight_golem:
Mechanical creations built by the ancient Starlighters to do the bidding of the mechanical giants used to defend against the doom, once possessing heavy armor and unparalleled strength.
To this day, no intact golems exist.
book.eternal_starlight.starlight_golem.d:
Under normal circumstances, its armor is difficult to penetrate.
However, when it stops attacking and begins to absorb energy, its weakness becomes apparent.
Simply extinguishing all the energy blocks it relies on will temporarily deactivate its armor.
book.eternal_starlight.starlight_golem.s: As an imperfect being, it does not move, which significantly lowers the difficulty of fighting it.
book.eternal_starlight.freeze:
In ancient times, they had been the embodiment of the frozen magic of this dimension. The discovery of the Freeze provided a major opportunity for the ancient Starlighters when they were building that mechanical giant and realized that the exothermic heat of the machine was too intense but could not be solved due to technical problems.
The Freeze were modified and eventually used successfully for cooling and defense against intruding enemies, and the magical ice ball they once shot were compressed and sealed in tubes.
book.eternal_starlight.freeze.attack: You can defend yourself against their intensive attacks using cold-proof armor.
book.eternal_starlight.permafrost:
Following the Starlighters' successful conversion of Freezes into cooling units, they soon realized the latent magical energy within these constructs far exceeded their initial projections. By fusing and augmenting multiple Freezes, they forged the ultimate thermal regulator: the Permafrost.
If the Freeze is a mere network of cooling vents, then the Permafrost is a surging pump of liquid nitrogen. As the definitive evolution of its predecessor, it retains the primal instincts of the Freeze while wielding absolute dominion over frost.
Long after the civilization crumbled into dust, this machine remains among the ruins, mechanically executing its final directive: to bring the world to absolute zero.
book.eternal_starlight.energy_transmitte:
The Energy Transmitter is a redstone device capable of transmitting redstone signal over long distances.
To use it, first interact with the emitter end, then with the receiver end to establish a connection between the two. Once linked, the Energy Transmitter will emit a beam of light between the emitter and receiver while active.
The emitter collects redstone signal from the block it is attached to and transmits them wirelessly, while the receiver passes the received signal to the block it is attached to.
book.eternal_starlight.accumulator:
The Accumulator is a redstone device that can receive redstone signal from one direction and output it in all other directions.
Among its six faces, the one marked with a red dot is the input face, while all other faces are output faces. As the input signal strengthens, the color of the Accumulator gradually shifts from gray to blue.
book.eternal_starlight.lunar_monstrosity: A plant infused with the power of the moon's radiance by an ancient civilization, used to devour the souls of prisoners held in the labyrinth.

Normally, its resilient epidermis significantly reduces all incoming damage.
However, when ignited or stunned, it loses this damage reduction ability.
As a plant, it remains immobile most of the time, but will occasionally burrow underground to pursue its prey.
book.eternal_starlight.tangled:
They are the remains of criminals imprisoned in the garden, whose life-force was not entirely consumed by the monstrosity, but overflowed outward to form a vegetative shell when their bodies were destroyed, a process considerably more painful than the devouring of their souls, a windfall which the ancient inhabitants were well pleased with, and which, as a matter of course, left the remains of these prisoners in the Labyrinth.
As their carapaces are broken, the souls within, overloaded by suffering, are released.
book.eternal_starlight.meteor_shower: Meteor showers sometimes occur here. During the meteor shower, countless meteors streak across the night sky, creating a beautiful sight. But there is also danger in the beauty, be careful not to get hit by the large meteorites. After dodging them, you can find some ores at the landing spot. Creteors may spawn after the large meteorites land, you can kill them to get their hide. You can also build an Aethersent Golem to prevent meteors from destroying your home, or use Aetherstrike Rockets to cause meteor showers manually.
book.eternal_starlight.thirst_walker:
They are the last descendants of ancient civilizations that were attacked by Gleeches. Their bodies were drained and then infected by starlight crystals. They are now as hungry as Gleeches for sustenance in this desert.
The unique structure of their teeth seems to allow them to store nutrients to increase their sharpness, and this holds true even after the teeth have left the Thirst Walker's body.
book.eternal_starlight.dagger_of_hunger:
A weapon crafted using the teeth of Thirst Walkers, the materials used to make it allow it to absorb nutrients to increase its sharpness.
It seems to retain activity and a primal need for food, so much so that he may act out and betray its master in cases of extreme hunger.
book.eternal_starlight.crystalborn_catal:
A machine that uses the teeth of Thirst Walkers as its core material, inheriting the Thirst Walker's greed.
Upon receiving a redstone signal, it can use the crystals in it to infest nearby environments and collect the resources contained therein.
book.eternal_starlight.stranghoul:
These bizarre humanoid creatures seem to have started popping up after that disaster. No one knows where they came from, and for some reason they are especially afraid of silver weapons.
While their habits are rather feral, they apparently have some intelligence and possess a tendency to create civilizations.
Their thin bodies make them more inclined to scavenging, but they will not turn away from dying people in their choice of food. They are fascinated by high-level rotten foods such as Pungency Stews, and because of this they will help anyone who gives it high-level rotten food for a certain amount of time.
They use Malarite to barter for items, so perhaps this could be used to obtain some valuable items from them?
book.eternal_starlight.pungency_fruit:
A fruit found everywhere in the Dark Swamp that tastes somewhat like garlic, it gives off an odor that makes people weep, which allows it to be made into a weapon as well.
A stew made of it and rotten flesh can rid you of hunger effect, but such food doesn't seem to be very tasty.
book.eternal_starlight.silver_pungency_f: A precious food made from Pungency Fruit and Deepsilver Ingots that still retains the flavor of Pungency Fruits. It paralyzes your nerves, causing your body to temporarily ignore most damage, but all damage is still returned after a period of time.
book.eternal_starlight.seeds_launcher:
This unique weapon can shoot seeds of any type at high speed, it is made primarily from Pungency Fruits, but the exact method of production is unknown, so the only way to obtain it is to barter with their makers.
The weapon can be enchanted, and when enchanted it can shoot seeds with unique properties.
book.eternal_starlight.drying_rack:
Stranghouls use it to dry rotten flesh into leather for their armor.
It can be placed over a campfire, at which point the rotten flesh can be placed to obtain Rotten Flesh Jerky, which is tastier but harder to chew than rotten flesh.
book.eternal_starlight.shimmer_lacewing: An insect that flits around shimmer river and dark swamp with four pairs of glowing blue or purple wings. Their presence is neither threatening nor useful to other creatures. When the Starlight civilization still existed, this was a small creature loved by children.
book.eternal_starlight.twilight_gaze: Twilight Gaze are known for their glowing purple eyes - in the Abyss, where they originate from, these eyes help them see their surroundings in total darkness. They love the environment of the Abyss, and will attempt to return to it if they stray too far from it. This fish will not actively attack humans, but if you harm them, the Twilight Gaze will not hesitate to fight back.
book.eternal_starlight.nocturnal_millet:
Nocturnal Millet is a crop native to the Starlight Dimension, whose seeds are hidden within Thioquartz at the banks of the Ether River.
Nocturnal Millet seeds can be sown on dirt, farmland, or Dusted Gravel. Once the stalks have grown, the tops will naturally produce panicles.
When the panicles are plump and ripe, interacting with or destroying them will grant Nocturnal Millet. The stalks will remain after harvesting, but there is also a small probability that they will wither. Withered Nocturnal Millet will continuously destroy other types of crops nearby. If a stalk loses its vitality, applying bone meal can revive it.
If Nocturnal Millet is planted on Dusted Gravel and bone meal is applied to the stalk, the entire plant will enter a state of forgotten. Panicles in this state no longer produce ordinary Nocturnal Millet, but instead condense into Forgotten Nocturnal Millet. Plants in the forgotten state will seize the life force of other types of crops nearby to accelerate their own maturation.
